p.scope-of-this-document: **Scope of this document.** Why a decision without a revisit condition rots into a sacred cow, what a measurable trigger is made of, good and bad trigger shapes, the periodic sweep that actually fires triggers, and the procedure when one fires.

p.record-shape-pointer: The record shape itself lives in [`record-template.md`](record-template.md).

p.EVERY-DECISION-IS-CORRECT-RELATIVE-TO-DA: Every decision is correct *relative to data*: 600 s is right while 15 % of users sit behind slow corporate VPNs.

p.data-changes-and-the-decision-outlives-i: Then the data changes — networks get faster, the library ships the missing feature, the compliance regime shifts — and the decision quietly outlives its reason.

p.two-failures-lead: Without a recorded revisit condition, one of two failures follows:

facts.FAILURE-THE-SACRED-COW: **The sacred cow.** The value is written down, so nobody dares question it. The reason expired long ago; the decision survives on the authority of being recorded. Recording — the thing meant to preserve reasoning — now preserves a fossil.
facts.FAILURE-THE-PERMANENT-RE-LITIGATION: **The permanent re-litigation.** The opposite failure: with no stated condition for reopening, every reader feels free to reopen at any time, and the record's immunity is worth nothing.

p.TRIGGER-FIXES-BOTH-AT-ONCE: The trigger fixes both at once.

p.TRIGGER-SAYS-THIS-DECISION-STANDS-UNTIL-: It tells every future reader *this decision stands until X* — which both forbids re-litigation before X and mandates it after.

p.NO-CONDITION-MEANS-A-SACRED-COW: A decision without a revisit condition becomes a sacred cow; a decision with one stays alive.

p.ALL-THREE-OR-IT-IS-NOT-A-TRIGGER: All three, or it is not a trigger.

p.why-each-of-the-three-parts-is-needed: A metric without a threshold cannot fire; a threshold without an observation point cannot be checked; an observation point nobody has is a wish.

p.EVENT-TRIGGERS-ARE-THE-SANCTIONED-NON-NU: **Event triggers** are the sanctioned variant for non-numeric conditions: an external event that is unambiguous when it happens.

p.event-trigger-examples: "A compliance requirement mandates a NIST-approved hash"; "upstream ships no release for 24 months"; "the vendor removes the v1 API".

p.EVENT-TRIGGERS-TAKE-THE-SAME-TEST: The test is the same — a stranger could answer yes-or-no today.

p.UNOBSERVABLE-TRIGGERS-ARE-AS-BAD-AS-NONE: **Unobservable triggers** are as bad as none.

p.COLLECT-THE-SIGNAL-OR-REWRITE-THE-TRIGGE: If the trigger names a metric the project does not collect, either start collecting it or rewrite the trigger against a signal that exists.

p.sweep-reports-unobservable-triggers: The periodic sweep below reports these explicitly.

td.ROW-TRIGGER-P99-LATENCY: "p99 delivery latency drops below 100 s, per the monitoring dashboard"

td.ROW-TRIGGER-HOT-PATH-CPU: "hot-path CPU exceeds 80 % in the weekly perf run"

td.fact: Fires from a run that already happens.
Event; checkable from the repository today.

td.ROW-TRIGGER-COMPLIANCE-MANDATE: "a compliance mandate requires a NIST-approved hash"

td.fact: Breakage is undefined and arrives too late to be a review.
Never fires. This is "revisit: never" in costume.
Names an unrelated activity, not a signal about *this* decision.
No metric, no threshold, no observer — pure vibes.

p.THE-MECHANICAL-TEST: The mechanical test: *"when it breaks" is not a trigger; a trigger is a measurable signal.*

p.THE-FIVE-MINUTE-STRANGER-TEST: If a stranger with access to the observation point could not answer "has it fired?" in five minutes, rewrite it.

periodic-sweep.title: The periodic sweep

p.nothing-pages-anyone-for-a-decision-grad: Nothing pages anyone when p99 crosses 100 s — unless the project wires an alert, and most decision-grade signals never earn one.

p.RE-READING-IS-WHAT-FIRES-TRIGGERS: The mechanism that actually fires triggers is **re-reading**, on a rhythm:

facts.RHYTHM-OPPORTUNISTIC: **Opportunistic:** whenever a session touches a document, glance at the triggers of the records in it. Cost: seconds.
facts.RHYTHM-PERIODIC: **Periodic:** weekly, or at each milestone close — whichever rhythm the project already keeps — sweep all records and check every trigger against current data. Delegate the sweep:

periodic-sweep.fence: Sweep the spec tree for decision records — sections carrying the Decision / Why / Considered and rejected / When to revisit fields. For each record: 1. Extract the revisit trigger. 2. Classify it against current data: fired / not fired / unobservable. Name the data source you checked, or the one you failed to find. 3. Edit nothing. Report a table: anchor, trigger, state, evidence. End with the list of unobservable triggers — each needs either a data source or a rewritten trigger. I will decide which records to reopen.

p.SWEEP-OUTPUT-IS-A-REVIEW-QUEUE-NOT-AN-ED: The sweep's output is a review queue, not an edit.

p.FIRING-A-TRIGGER-IS-A-HUMAN-DECISION-POI: Firing a trigger is a human decision-point, because what fires is a *question*, not an answer.

p.RE-OPEN-THE-RECORD-NEVER-SILENTLY-EDIT-T: Re-open the record — do not silently edit the value.

p.the-failure-to-avoid: The failure to avoid: the constant changes in code, the record keeps the old why, and the spec now testifies to a reason that no longer produced the value.

p.drift-manufactured-where-it-was-to-be-pr: That is drift manufactured at the exact point built to prevent it.

facts.STEP-NAME-THE-FIRED-STATE: **Name the fired state.** "The trigger fired: p99 has been at 82 s for three consecutive weeks, per the dashboard." This sentence opens the re-litigation legitimately — and it is the only thing that does.
facts.STEP-RE-RUN-THE-DECISION-WITH-CURRENT-DA: **Re-run the decision with current data.** The old rejected alternatives get first look: their rejection reasons may have expired along with the trigger.
facts.OUTCOME-REAFFIRMED: **Reaffirmed.** The decision stands on new data. Refresh the why with the new evidence and set a *new* trigger — a fired trigger is spent.
facts.OUTCOME-CHANGED: **Changed.** Rewrite the record in place — new decision, new why, new rejections (the old winner joins them, with its reason), new trigger. Add a dated line to the document's version history. Git keeps the old text.
facts.STEP-COMMIT-CITING-THE-ANCHOR: **Commit citing the anchor.** The commit body names the trigger state that opened the record and cites the record's anchor; the spec carries the reasoning, the commit points at it.

p.NEVER-DELETE-A-RECORD-REWRITE-IT: Never delete a record when a decision changes — rewrite it.

p.why-rewriting-keeps-citations-live: The anchor stays stable, every citation into it stays live, and the superseded reasoning remains one `git log -p` away.

facts.SUM-NO-CONDITION-MEANS-A-SACRED-COW: A decision without a revisit condition becomes a sacred cow — or a permanent re-litigation target. The trigger prevents both.
facts.SUM-WHAT-A-TRIGGER-IS-MADE-OF: A trigger is metric + threshold + observation point, or an unambiguous external event. "Later" and "when it breaks" are not triggers.
facts.SUM-UNOBSERVABLE-TRIGGERS-ARE-AS-BAD-AS-: Unobservable triggers are as bad as none: collect the signal or rewrite the trigger.
facts.SUM-TRIGGERS-FIRE-BY-BEING-RE-READ: Triggers fire by being re-read: opportunistically on touch, periodically by sweep. Delegate the sweep; keep the reopening decision human.
facts.SUM-A-FIRED-TRIGGER-RE-OPENS-THE-RECORD: A fired trigger re-opens the record, never silently edits the value. Reaffirm with a fresh why and a new trigger, or rewrite in place with a changelog line. Git is the history.
